note: Create the trigger function that keeps amount and total identical: on INSERT it fills whichever of the two the app did not write; on UPDATE it copies whichever side changed to the other. No table lock needed.

Expand: add nullable column total (metadata-only, no rewrite) and the sync trigger in one transaction. The lock is taken with a 500 ms lock_timeout and retried, so app queries never queue behind it for long (app statement timeout is 2 s).
Backfill ids [1, 2M) in batches of 20k, committing each batch (short row locks, the app never updates orders anyway).
Vacuum so the dead row versions from the backfill are reused instead of growing the table.
Backfill ids [2M, 4M).
Vacuum.
Backfill ids [4M, 6M).
Vacuum.
Backfill ids [6M, 8M).
Vacuum.
Backfill ids [8M, max(id)]: everything up to the current max, which covers any row inserted before the trigger existed (later rows are filled by the trigger).
Vacuum and refresh statistics.
Check: every row has total equal to amount. Fails the plan (before any app change) if not.
NOT NULL on total without a long lock, step 1: add CHECK (total IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID (brief lock, retried).
Step 2: validate the check. Takes only SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, so reads and inserts continue during the scan.
Step 3: SET NOT NULL uses the validated check and skips the table scan, so the lock is momentary; then drop the now-redundant check.
Switch the app to total. During the rolling update old pods read/write amount and new pods read/write total; the trigger keeps both columns filled and equal for every insert.
